children.name: Article Lead
children.text: Translate a game template’s schema into safe player-facing settings, runtime flags, and memory values before creation.

children.name: Article Callout Text
children.text: World identity and authentication choices are easiest to correct before the first boot and persistent data creation.

children.name: Section Body 1
children.text: Separate infrastructure identity, operator description, and multiplayer-browser messaging.

children.name: Section 1 Item Text 0
children.text: Use a lowercase dash-separated name; it becomes workload identity.

children.name: Section 1 Item Text 1
children.text: Keep description operational and configure MOTD separately.

children.name: Section 1 Item Text 2
children.text: Set maximum players from realistic CPU, memory, and network capacity.

children.name: Section Body 2
children.text: Choose difficulty, game mode, PvP, hardcore, whitelist, seed, and identity verification for the intended community.

children.name: Section 2 Item Text 0
children.text: Record a deliberate seed before first boot; later changes do not rewrite a world.

children.name: Section 2 Item Text 1
children.text: Keep online mode enabled unless the server is intentionally isolated.

children.name: Section 2 Item Text 2
children.text: Review whitelist and hardcore consequences before creating persistent data.

children.name: Section Body 3
children.text: Prefer automatic heap sizing; when pinning JVM values, preserve non-heap headroom and keep credentials in Secret references.

children.name: Quick Reference Line 1
children.text: 01  Confirm infrastructure name, description, MOTD, and player limit

children.name: Quick Reference Line 2
children.text: 02  Confirm game rules, whitelist, identity mode, and world seed

children.name: Quick Reference Line 3
children.text: 03  Prefer auto heap; if pinned, leave ~25% headroom and review YAML

children.name: Edit Page Body
children.text: Found a gap? Open a docs issue or suggest an edit on GitHub.
